mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.2%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months) signals an imminent monetary tightening, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, the subsequent 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in one month signals strong economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.2pp and HOUST rises > 10% in 1 month
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls > 0.2pp and HOUST rises > 10% in 1 month, the subsequent 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in residential sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, when RSAFS declines, the subsequent 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently high unemployment rate (above 8%) compresses corporate profit margins and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is above 8%, the subsequent 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 (index, 2017=100) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 90, the subsequent 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% and a rise in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% signals an inflationary monetary policy response, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 2.5 and FEDFUNDS > 0.5, the subsequent 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation and supply constraints, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation and supply constraints, when INDPRO < 90, the subsequent 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
